sections.title: Domain 2: Implementation and Integration

keyTerms.definition: Programs that call models and tools, remember context, and carry out multi-step work.
The APIs, integrations, and infrastructure that turn a model into a working product.

recall.question: What is the difference between Domain 1 and Domain 2?
recall.answer: Domain 1 was design. Domain 2 is the build: agents, APIs, and the plumbing that turn a model into a product.

sections.title: How to use this volume

keyTerms.definition: AWS exam questions of 3 to 6 sentences with hard constraints you must satisfy.
A wrong answer choice that violates exactly one constraint of the scenario.

recall.question: How do you pick the right answer on an AWS scenario question?
recall.answer: Map each constraint to one architectural choice. The correct answer satisfies every constraint, and each distractor violates exactly one.

sections.title: 1. The Converse API: one interface for every model

keyTerms.definition: The unified Bedrock inference API with one request shape for Claude, Llama, Titan, and Nova.
The Converse field that describes each tool's name, description, and input schema.
The model's structured request block asking your application to run a named tool.
The block your application sends back with the outcome of a tool execution.
The Converse field naming the model: a base ID, an inference profile, or a provisioned model ARN.

recall.question: Why is Converse better than InvokeModel for multi-provider apps?
recall.answer: Converse has one request shape across providers, so the model ID becomes a configuration value and switching models needs no code rewrite.

recall.question: In the Converse tool-use loop, who runs the tool?
recall.answer: Your application runs the code and returns a toolResult. The model only emits a structured toolUse request and never executes code.

recall.question: Why can Converse not generate embeddings?
recall.answer: Converse is text generation only. Embeddings need InvokeModel with an embedding model like Titan Text Embeddings.

sections.title: 2. InvokeModel, provider specifics, and prompt caching

keyTerms.definition: The raw Bedrock API that takes each provider's native request body and supports embeddings.
A list of numbers capturing a text's meaning; similar meanings get similar numbers for search.
Reusing the computation for a repeated prompt prefix so later calls bill cached tokens at a discount.
Time to live: 5 minutes by default for a cache, with a 1-hour option on supported models.
The error a wrong provider body returns; always a request bug, never a model bug.

recall.question: When must you use InvokeModel instead of Converse?
recall.answer: Use InvokeModel for provider-native features Converse cannot express: embeddings, the newest sampling parameters, and provider-specific bodies.

recall.question: What breaks prompt caching?
recall.answer: The prefix must match exactly, token for token, up to the cache point. One changed character invalidates the cache, so put volatile content after it.

recall.question: How does prompt caching save money?
recall.answer: The first call pays a write surcharge. Later calls with the same prefix read cached tokens at about 10 percent of the input price within the TTL.

sections.title: 3. Long-running and non-interactive inference: asynchronous and batch

keyTerms.definition: Submit one request, get a job ID, and poll or get notified when the background result lands in S3.
One job that processes many prompts from S3 over hours at about half the on-demand price.
Delivering tokens to a waiting user in real time through ConverseStream and WebSockets.
The identifier returned by start_async_invoke for tracking one async request.
Reserved model capacity for steady baselines with latency and throughput guarantees.

recall.question: When is batch inference the right choice?
recall.answer: When no one waits for individual results and hours of latency are fine, like nightly summarization. Batch costs about 50 percent less.

recall.question: How do async, batch, and streaming differ?
recall.answer: Batch is many prompts from S3 over hours. Async is one slow prompt nobody waits on with the result in S3. Streaming sends tokens to a waiting user.

recall.question: Why can batch inference not serve sub-3-second responses?
recall.answer: Batch latency is measured in hours by design. No batch tuning reaches 3 seconds, so interactive latency needs real-time inference.

sections.title: 4. Prompt management: engineering discipline for prompts

keyTerms.definition: Alternate prompt forms for A/B comparison, such as formal versus friendly tone.
Immutable prompt releases; rollback means pointing at an older version.
The no-code visual builder that chains prompts into multi-step workflows with branching.
The craft of system prompts, few-shot examples, chain-of-thought, and structured output.

recall.question: Variants or versions: which is for A/B testing and which for rollback?
recall.answer: Variants compare alternatives side by side. Versions are immutable releases, and rollback means pointing at an older version.

recall.question: How does Prompt Management differ from prompt caching?
recall.answer: Management organizes prompts with versions, variants, and no redeploys. Caching makes repeated prompts cheaper. Change-frequency points to Management.

sections.title: 5. Knowledge Bases: grounding answers in your documents

keyTerms.definition: Retrieval-augmented generation: retrieve first, then generate, pasting retrieved passages into the prompt.
Splitting documents into small passages before embedding so each embedding captures one meaning.
The database holding chunk embeddings plus text and source metadata for nearest-vector search.
The one managed Knowledge Base call that retrieves, builds the prompt, generates, and cites.
How many chunks return from the vector search; too few starves the answer, too many adds noise.
Meaning-vectors from text; similar meanings produce similar numbers for nearest-vector search.

recall.question: What are the two phases of the RAG pipeline?
recall.answer: Ingest runs offline when documents change: chunk, embed, store. Query runs online per question: embed the question, search top-k, generate with citations.

recall.question: A RAG system gives confident but wrong answers. What do you fix first?
recall.answer: Fix retrieval: the chunking strategy, the embedding model, and top-k. A bigger model cannot rescue passages that were never retrieved.

recall.question: When should you use Retrieve instead of RetrieveAndGenerate?
recall.answer: Use Retrieve when you need your own reranking step, a custom prompt template, or a strict citation format the managed call lacks.

sections.title: 6. Bedrock Agents: Anatomy of an Agent

keyTerms.definition: The tools an agent can call, each running Lambda code or an external API from an OpenAPI schema.
The call that compiles agent configuration changes from DRAFT to PREPARED.
The invoke_agent flag returning the agent's reasoning trace for transparency and debugging.
The invoke_agent key that gives the agent memory across turns in a conversation.
The system-level prompt telling the agent its role and how to behave.

recall.question: You changed an agent's configuration but it behaves as before. What is wrong?
recall.answer: The change stays in DRAFT until you run prepare-agent. Prepare the agent, test it, then repoint the alias at the prepared version.

recall.question: What four things does a Bedrock Agent add to a foundation model?
recall.answer: An agent instruction, action groups for tools, a knowledge base for grounding, and guardrails for safety, plus an IAM role.

recall.question: How do auditors see an agent's step-by-step reasoning?
recall.answer: Set enableTrace on invoke_agent. It returns the orchestration trace showing which tools the agent chose and why.

sections.title: 7. Multi-agent collaboration: supervisor, collaborators, and open frameworks

keyTerms.definition: The agent that routes subtasks to specialists and composes the final answer.
A full specialist agent with its own instruction, action groups, and knowledge base.
The setting controlling how much conversation context a collaborator sees; it trades tokens for context.
The open-source, code-first SDK for building agents in Python.
A Step Functions approval step that gates risky agent actions above a threshold.

recall.question: How does a supervisor talk to its collaborators?
recall.answer: Through the built-in supervisor and collaborator delegation mechanism, never through action groups, which are agent-to-tool only.

recall.question: Why must you prepare and alias collaborators?
recall.answer: A supervisor cannot delegate to a DRAFT collaborator. When the supervisor never delegates, the fix is prepare plus alias.

recall.question: What is the cost risk in multi-agent delegation?
recall.answer: Token cost scales with delegation depth and history relay. A 20-turn session can carry 40,000 tokens, so tune relay-conversation-history.

sections.title: 8. Agents with Knowledge Bases and Guardrails: the holy trinity

keyTerms.definition: Subject areas blocked in plain language, such as investment advice or medical diagnosis.
Guardrail controls blocking toxicity categories like hate or violence at severity thresholds.
The guardrail screen that checks the user message before any model call.
Personally identifiable information that sensitive information filters can block or mask.
The invoke_agent flag whose traces show which KB chunks were used and which guardrail rules fired.

recall.question: In one invoke_agent call, what is the fixed order of the trinity?
recall.answer: Input guardrail screens the user message first, then the KB-grounded agent loop runs, then the output guardrail screens the final answer.

recall.question: Do guardrails extract content from documents?
recall.answer: No. Guardrails filter content. Extraction is Bedrock Data Automation or a KB with the right chunking.

sections.title: 9. Lambda integration patterns: sync, async, streaming, timeouts, concurrency

keyTerms.definition: Synchronous Lambda invocation where the caller waits for the result.
Asynchronous Lambda invocation: Lambda queues the event and returns immediately.
Capacity guaranteed for one function so critical work always has room.
Warm instances kept ready to remove cold starts, billed even when idle.
The queue that catches events after Lambda's retries are exhausted.

recall.question: A chatbot streams 90-second answers and users see timeouts, but the Lambda timeout is 5 minutes. What is the real limit?
recall.answer: The API Gateway REST 29-second integration timeout. The fix is WebSockets or async with polling, not a bigger Lambda timeout.

recall.question: How do you size concurrency for a GenAI API?
recall.answer: Concurrent executions equal requests per second times seconds per request. Ten requests per second at 8 seconds each needs 80 concurrent executions.

recall.question: Can a Lambda wait for human approval?
recall.answer: No. Lambda caps at 15 minutes, so use Step Functions Standard with waitForTaskToken for approvals and long waits.

sections.title: 10. API Gateway in front of Bedrock

keyTerms.definition: Per-client tiers that set rate limits and throttle each API key on the gateway.
A Lambda function that validates the caller's token before the request reaches the handler.
The API Gateway REST integration timeout that kills long model calls regardless of the Lambda timeout.
The service holding the model ID as runtime configuration so Lambda can switch models without redeploys.
Per-route and per-API-key limits that protect Bedrock quotas from one noisy client.

recall.question: Why put API Gateway in front of Bedrock instead of calling Bedrock from clients?
recall.answer: The gateway URL stays fixed so model changes never touch clients, and it adds central throttling, authentication, and per-client rate control.

recall.question: How do you switch between Claude, Titan, and Llama without redeploying clients or code?
recall.answer: AppConfig holds the model ID as runtime configuration, Lambda routes on it, and API Gateway gives clients one stable URL.

sections.title: 11. Step Functions Orchestration of GenAI Workflows

keyTerms.definition: The sequence of steps Step Functions runs: tasks, choices, waits, and parallel branches.
Step Functions type running up to one year with exactly-once semantics for long GenAI pipelines.
Step Functions type capped at 5 minutes with at-least-once semantics for short, high-volume runs.
The callback pattern that pauses an execution until an approval click resumes it.
Choice states that check failure counts or confidence scores and route to a fallback.
A counter or max-iterations Choice guard that ends agent-style loops before they burn budget.

recall.question: A workflow must pause 48 hours for manager approval, then resume. What do you use?
recall.answer: Step Functions Standard with waitForTaskToken. The approver's click calls SendTaskSuccess or SendTaskFailure and the execution resumes.

recall.question: When do you use Standard versus Express?
recall.answer: Standard runs up to one year with exactly-once semantics for approvals and waits. Express caps at 5 minutes with at-least-once semantics for short high-volume work.

recall.question: How do you stop a pipeline from retrying a failing model call forever?
recall.answer: Add a Choice state as a circuit breaker with a max-attempts stopping condition that routes to a fallback.

sections.title: 12. S3 and EventBridge: Event-Driven GenAI Pipelines

keyTerms.definition: The S3 event notification fired when a file lands, routed by EventBridge to processing.
The no-code connector that filters and enriches data between an event source and a target.
The queue that parks poison messages after a bounded number of failures for inspection.
Keeping every version of every object for audit and rollback.
The window a message stays hidden while processing; set it longer than the processing time.

recall.question: Why is CloudTrail the wrong trigger for file-arrival processing?
recall.answer: CloudTrail records API calls for audit. S3 event notifications plus EventBridge move data. Match the tool to the plane: audit versus data flow.

recall.question: One malformed PDF crashes extraction on every retry and blocks the queue. What is the fix?
recall.answer: Route to a dead-letter queue after a bounded number of attempts. Healthy files keep flowing and the bad file can be inspected.

sections.title: 13. Model deployment strategies: on-demand, Provisioned Throughput, SageMaker, cascading

keyTerms.definition: Reserved model units for 1 to 6 month terms with dedicated capacity and no throttling.
Pay-per-token inference on shared capacity for spiky, experimental, or unpredictable traffic.
The exam-favorite pattern: Provisioned Throughput for the baseline plus on-demand for spikes.
A router sending simple requests to a cheap model and escalating only complex ones to the flagship.
Self-hosting for custom models with real-time endpoints, autoscaling, and async inference.

recall.question: The team bought Provisioned Throughput but still sees throttling. What is the likely bug?
recall.answer: The code calls invoke_model with the base model ID instead of the provisioned model ARN. Route to the provisioned ARN to fix it.

recall.question: 2M requests per day, a steady baseline, 10x Friday spikes, and a sub-3s SLA. What deployment?
recall.answer: Hybrid: buy Provisioned Throughput for the baseline and route Friday overflow to on-demand. Pure on-demand throttles and peak-sized PT wastes capacity.

sections.title: 14. Enterprise integration: legacy systems, secure access, and the GenAI gateway

keyTerms.definition: The centralized front door for all model access with policy, observability, and cost control.
Role-based access control for which teams and roles can use which models and data.
The VPC endpoint that lets a corporate app reach Bedrock without crossing the public internet.
The service whose permission sets scope each tenant's application to its own resources.
AWS hardware on-prem for data-residency and ultra-low-latency constraints.

recall.question: How do you isolate 40 hotel properties' data in one GenAI assistant?
recall.answer: Use one knowledge base per property with IAM Identity Center permission sets. Prompts are not access control, so never use one shared KB with prompt-level isolation.

recall.question: What three jobs does a GenAI gateway do?
recall.answer: Enforce policy on which models and guardrails, provide observability and per-team cost attribution, and abstract model swaps without client changes.

sections.title: 15. Application patterns: chatbots, copilots, Q&A over documents, and Bedrock Data Automation

keyTerms.definition: Bedrock Data Automation: the managed service extracting text, tables, and structure from documents, images, video, and audio.
The store for chatbot session state: millisecond keyed reads with TTL expiry per conversation.
The Amazon Q chat assistant for employees over company wikis and tickets.
The Amazon Q IDE assistant for code generation and refactoring.
The declarative UI framework for building chat front ends on AWS.

recall.question: Where does chatbot conversation state live: DynamoDB or S3?
recall.answer: DynamoDB, keyed by conversation ID with TTL. S3 has higher latency and the wrong access pattern for per-turn reads.

recall.question: Q Business or Q Developer: which is the IDE coding assistant?
recall.answer: Q Developer is for developers needing code generation and refactoring in the IDE. Q Business is the chat assistant over company data.

sections.title: 16. Embed Bedrock in existing applications: SDKs, retries, and reliability

keyTerms.definition: The AWS SDK client for inference: Converse and InvokeModel.
The normal-at-scale Bedrock signal for quota pressure, handled with backoff, not treated as a bug.
Retries that wait 1 second, then 2, then 4, with jitter so a fleet does not retry in lockstep.
The pattern that opens after repeated failures so calls fail fast instead of hammering Bedrock.
The distributed tracing that shows which hop is slow across API Gateway, Lambda, Bedrock, and the KB.

recall.question: An app gets throttles at peak. What is the correct retry strategy?
recall.answer: Use exponential backoff with jitter and a maximum-attempts ceiling, then a fallback model or cached response. Never retry in a tight loop.

recall.question: AccessDeniedException on a new model in a new region. What do you check first?
recall.answer: Check whether the model is available in that region first, then the IAM policy. AccessDenied does not always mean a bad policy.

sections.title: Master trap list: Domain 2

keyTerms.definition: The step teams skip when an agent ignores new configuration; prepare, then re-alias.
Agent-to-tool connectors; the exam is wrong when it wires agents together through them.

recall.question: What is the fix when an agent ignores a new action group?
recall.answer: The team skipped prepare-agent. Run prepare-agent to compile DRAFT to PREPARED, then repoint the alias.

sections.title: Question bank: Domain 2

keyTerms.definition: The unified Bedrock API across providers; the correct pick for same-code multi-provider tool use.
The cost fix when every call resends a long stable prefix like a product catalog.
The first check when an agent keeps old behavior after an instruction change.
The Step Functions Standard pattern for durable multi-day approval pauses.
Where poison messages go after bounded retries so healthy files keep flowing.

recall.question: Which API is the only one that supports embedding models?
recall.answer: InvokeModel. Converse and ConverseStream only generate text, and ApplyGuardrail is a safety API.

recall.question: The team bought Provisioned Throughput but still throttles while calling invoke_model with the base model ID. What is the fix?
recall.answer: Route invocations to the provisioned model ARN. Calling the base model ID bypasses the purchased capacity.

recall.question: What is the maximum execution time for one Lambda invocation?
recall.answer: 15 minutes. The 29-second limit is the API Gateway REST integration timeout, and 5 minutes is the Step Functions Express maximum.
